https://northshield.org/calendar/1538/: Each person coming to our event is given tokens to try both indoor and outdoor games. Each person playing a game contributes the token and the winner of the games will be the person with the most tokens. If you run out of tokens you can gain more by doing a bardic performance or a pledge of service to get more. The person with the most tokens wins by the end of the day. We are looking for instructors to teach classes on different A&S topics. Alcohol and open fire demonstrations are welcome. Please contact Xene (Johnny Kruse). Teaching and attending classes will get you a token. Depending on interest and marshal availability we have plenty of space to start a few fighting games as well in period rapier and/or armored combat. Archery; Depending on marshal availability another way to get tokens. Bring your gear. We encourage people to bring some medieval games and projects to work on during the event. Different games planned include board games, Bocce, and Quoits. Fighting and archery tournaments to win coins as well. https://northshield.org/calendar/1542/: Camp Sinawa is a beautiful campground with ample tent space and cabins that will be available for rent. We are planning on having rattan fighting, rapier, youth combat, archery, thrown weapons, classes, artisans’ row, and bardic activities. If people are inclined, they can do some Viking Hiking on the many trails around the camp. Outside food and drinks are permitted. A breakfast has been served in the past for a fee on Saturday morning. Showers on-site in the bath house and bunk houses. ADA accessible bunkhouse has a shared kitchen space with refrigerator, stove, and microwave. Bunkhouse and cabins have bunk beds and campers need to supply their own bedding, sheets, pillows, and blankets. Site is discretely wet – original containers must be out of sight. Service animals only. No smoking inside any building. NO driving on the grass for any reason. Campers must carry their own gear or use a wagon to transport anything to their campsite. Quiet hours for the upper campground after 10 PM. https://northshield.org/calendar/1579/: There will be armoured combat, rapier, possible youth combat (if there is interest and someone to marshal), archery, thrown weapons, A&S classes, war court, Royal court. Site is a discreetly wet site. There is no cannabis allowed to be smoked on site and must be consumed off site on the road as per site rules. It is rustic accessible in terms of wheelchair and disability accessibility. All door have lips, and the paths are gravel or uneven. Some buildings do not have ramps. ( please be note if a ramp is needed). The cabins have power but not many outlets so again please let us know if you need an outlet. Tenting is available, and there is limited space for RVs. Any RV parking will not be powered. At this time I have an A&S contest planned : Make a band (length of weaving, bracelet, crocheted etc) containing many colors as a nod to the fourth Doctor’s scarf. Her excellency the Baroness has issued the call for the A&S community to bring her the skulls of her enemies yet again. There will also be a written bardic competition planned: Entitled, tell me your story. It should be in written form no more than 1000 words ( think newspaper article). The topic of the piece can either be your persona’s back story or how you joined the SCA. Winners will be determined by a popular bean count vote. Entries will be printed in the chronicle throughout the fall/ winter seasons following the event. There will be the option to opt out if people would like. Please note: While dogs are allowed onsite they are note allowed in ANY building, and must be on-leash. Please plan accordingly. https://northshield.org/calendar/1580/: This event is named after the official DND cookbook, Hero’s Feast, and we will be posting recipes from the book for anyone who’d like to make and bring one. Recipes are also welcome from Redwall and Lord of the Rings this year. There is a cooking competition as part of the feast, and the winner is dubbed the Beast of the Feast. There are also multiple tournaments with a prize for the winner of the Cut and Thrust tournament! This event is extremely low key and full of schtick. There will also be a bonfire and a bardic circle afterwards. Tournament Format: 1. The Novice Hero’s Tourney – This competition is for our up and coming fighters with a glove at the upper limit of who is allowed to fight, it will be in the style of a round Robin. Those without a glove have 2 lives and those with a glove have 1. 2. The Cut & Thrust Tourney – This competition is for the title of “Beast Slayer” and is exclusively a C&T armor as worn tournament. 3. The Legends Tournament – Fight as a randomly assigned hero with different abilities and abilities! Each Tourney has it’s own exclusive prize! May the best hero win! Limited crash space is available, contact the event steward for more details From 9am to 4pm, we will be at the Pierre Masonic Temple for fighting, and then from 4pm to 10pm we will be at the Farr House up the road for feasting.
